# Code Review — 2026-07-14

- [ ] **[Security] Separate worker credentials from full-access client credentials**
  - **Status quo:** One `ServerConfig.Token` authenticates every API route, including file writes, allowlisted destructive commands, and worker lease/complete/fail operations (`internal/selfhost/server.go:130`, `internal/selfhost/server.go:144`); deployment instructions explicitly give apps and remote workers the same token (`README.md:97`, `README.md:113`). A worker credential therefore grants substantially more authority than OCR processing requires.
  - **Proposed solution:** Introduce distinct, rotatable client/admin and worker tokens with route-level scopes; keep a documented compatibility window in which the legacy token maps to both scopes, add authorization-matrix tests for every route, and update Compose/Home Assistant examples to provision separate secrets.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Medium effort / high impact

- [ ] **[Security] Pin privileged GitHub Actions to immutable commit SHAs**
  - **Status quo:** Release and container workflows grant repository/package write access and consume signing or publishing secrets, but actions are referenced by mutable major tags such as `goreleaser/goreleaser-action@v7` and `softprops/action-gh-release@v3` (`.github/workflows/release.yml:8`, `.github/workflows/release.yml:59`, `.github/workflows/release.yml:260`, `.github/workflows/container.yml:18`).
  - **Proposed solution:** Pin every workflow action to a reviewed full commit SHA while retaining the release tag in a comment, and keep the existing GitHub Actions Dependabot entry to propose auditable SHA updates.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Low effort / high impact

- [ ] **[UX/DX] Preserve true streaming for remote AI operations**
  - **Status quo:** The server buffers up to 32 MiB of subprocess stdout and sends it only after completion (`internal/selfhost/server.go:400`, `internal/selfhost/server.go:405`, `internal/selfhost/server.go:423`); the macOS client then splits that completed response into an `AsyncThrowingStream` (`Sources/SymDeskCore/DeskCore.swift:745`, `Sources/SymDeskCore/DeskCore.swift:749`). Remote users therefore see no incremental answer and cannot meaningfully cancel a long AI request.
  - **Proposed solution:** Add an authenticated chunked NDJSON/SSE execution path for `ask` and `transform`, flush validated events as they arrive, propagate cancellation to `exec.CommandContext`, and cover first-byte latency, malformed chunks, cancellation, and non-zero process exits with HTTP integration tests.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Medium effort / high impact

- [ ] **[UX/DX] Surface failed mutations instead of silently advancing UI state**
  - **Status quo:** Several user-triggered mutations discard errors with `try?` or console-only logging; view deletion clears selection even when deletion fails, conflict resolution clears the selected note, and queue retry immediately refreshes without feedback (`Sources/SymDeskApp/ContentView.swift:157`, `Sources/SymDeskApp/ContentView.swift:247`, `Sources/SymDeskApp/UI/IngestQueueView.swift:103`). This can make failed or destructive actions appear successful.
  - **Proposed solution:** Route mutations through a reusable async action state that exposes progress and an alert/banner, update local state only after confirmed success, retain the target on failure for retry, and add UI-facing tests for failed delete, conflict resolution, save, ingest, and retry paths.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Low effort / high impact

- [ ] **[Architecture] Isolate local CLI and remote HTTP transports behind one tested contract**
  - **Status quo:** The 1,097-line `DeskCore` combines shared DTOs, app state, local process orchestration, remote branching, decoding, and feature methods (`Sources/SymDeskCore/DeskCore.swift:515`, `Sources/SymDeskCore/DeskCore.swift:603`); special-case transport branches recur across ingest, AI, jobs, and file access (`Sources/SymDeskCore/DeskCore.swift:698`, `Sources/SymDeskCore/DeskCore.swift:719`, `Sources/SymDeskCore/DeskCore.swift:934`). Existing Swift tests cover URL normalization but not `RemoteDeskClient` HTTP behavior (`Tests/SymDeskCoreTests/DeskCoreTests.swift:499`).
  - **Proposed solution:** Define a narrow `DeskTransport` protocol for command, streaming, file, ingest, and job operations; implement CLI and HTTP transports, inject the transport into a smaller observable facade, move DTOs into contract-focused files, and run the same behavioral contract tests against fakes for both modes.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Medium effort / high impact

- [ ] **[Performance] Make remote mobile refresh conditional and incrementally invalidated**
  - **Status quo:** Every snapshot request walks and stats the complete Markdown vault to derive an ETag (`internal/selfhost/server.go:208`, `internal/selfhost/server.go:211`), while the mobile client never sends `If-None-Match` and reparses every note from the full response on each reload (`Sources/SymDeskMobile/MobileServerConnection.swift:115`, `Sources/SymDeskMobile/MobileServerConnection.swift:124`, `Sources/SymDeskMobile/MobileVault.swift:436`). This repeats O(n) server work and a full client parse even when the vault is unchanged, and no unchanged-refresh benchmark or mobile HTTP test covers the path.
  - **Proposed solution:** Persist the last ETag and decoded mobile snapshot, send `If-None-Match`, treat `304` as a cache hit, and replace per-request server walks with a revision/cache invalidated by API writes plus the existing vault watcher; add a 10k-note refresh benchmark for unchanged and single-note-change cases.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Medium effort / high impact

## Conclusion

The first recommended quick win is pinning privileged GitHub Actions to immutable SHAs: it is a small, isolated change that immediately reduces release supply-chain risk.
